# Unbound Force: Evaluation for Claude Code Workflow Integration

A citation-backed evaluation of [Unbound Force](https://unboundforce.dev/) —
an AI agent swarm ecosystem for software engineering — across architecture,
components, Claude Code compatibility, alternatives, maturity, and adoption risk.

## Methodology

All claims in this document trace to web sources visited in-session. Sources
are numbered and detailed in [citations.md](citations.md). Per-dimension
reference files in [references/](references/) contain the full data. Two
independent review agents audited this document after completion:
[citation audit](audit/citation-audit.md) and
[consistency review](audit/consistency-review.md).

---

## Executive Summary

Unbound Force is a 2-month-old, single-maintainer (bus factor = 1 [13])
multi-agent development ecosystem built on OpenCode [2]. It provides three
genuinely novel capabilities:

1. **Contract coverage** (Gaze) — measures whether tests assert on what
   functions promise, not just what they execute [11][7]
2. **Persistent knowledge graph** (Dewey) — 48-tool MCP server with semantic
   search, trust tiers, and knowledge lifecycle management [6][10]
3. **Structured multi-agent coordination** (Replicator) — 53-tool MCP server
   for work tracking, messaging, and git worktree orchestration [9][5]

**For a Claude Code user**: The full stack requires OpenCode and is not
adoptable [8][18]. However, Replicator and Dewey are MCP-portable to Claude
Code [9], and Gaze works as a standalone CLI for Go projects [11]. The
primary adoption barrier is not compatibility — it's the project's critical
maturity risks: bus factor of 1, near-zero community (1 GitHub star total),
and rapid API instability (Dewey: 3 major versions in 14 days) [12][13][14].

## 1. Architecture

Unbound Force operates as a three-layer stack [2]:

| Layer | Component | Role |
|-------|-----------|------|
| Agent | OpenCode [19] | AI coding environment (TUI, 75+ models) |
| Planning | Speckit / OpenSpec [8] | Specification pipelines (strategic + tactical) |
| Coordination | Replicator [9] | Multi-agent orchestration (MCP, 53 tools) |

A knowledge layer (Dewey [6]) and a test quality tool (Gaze [11]) support
the stack. The whole system is governed by a constitution [3] with four
mandatory principles (Autonomous Collaboration, Composability First,
Observable Quality, Testability) enforced via a Constitution Check gate.

Five AI personas ("heroes") fill development roles [8]: Muti-Mind (Product
Owner), Cobalt-Crush (Developer), Gaze (Tester), The Divisor (PR Reviewer),
and Mx F (Manager). All are listed as Implemented.

See [references/architecture.md](references/architecture.md) for full details.

## 2. Components

### Gaze — Contract Coverage for Go

The most novel and standalone component. Gaze detects 37 effect types across
5 tiers (P0-P4), classifies them as contractual vs incidental, and measures
whether tests assert on the contractual ones [11][7].

Three metrics [7]:
- **Contract Coverage**: % of contractual effects verified (Good ≥80%)
- **Over-Specification Score**: assertions on implementation details (Bad >3)
- **GazeCRAP**: complexity² × (1 - contractCoverage)³ + complexity

Current assertion mapping accuracy: ~84.7% (target: 90%) [7]. P3-P4 effects
(stdout, environment, mutex, reflection) not yet detected [7].

### Dewey — Knowledge Graph MCP Server

Hard fork of [Graphthulhu](https://github.com/skridlevsky/graphthulhu) (39
tools, 133 stars [15]), extended to 48 tools with persistent SQLite, semantic
search via IBM Granite embeddings through Ollama, and 4 content sources
(Markdown, GitHub, web crawl, Go code) [10][6].

Knowledge lifecycle management: Compile (synthesize learnings), Lint (detect
quality issues), Promote (advance trust tiers: draft → validated → authored)
[6].

### Replicator — Multi-Agent Coordination

Go rewrite of cyborg-swarm (TypeScript) [9]. 53 MCP tools across 4 categories:
Org/Hive (11, work tracking), Comms/Swarm Mail (10, messaging + file
reservations), Forge/Swarm (24, decomposition + worktrees), Memory (8, Dewey
proxy) [9][5]. ~15MB binary, <50ms startup, 190+ tests [9].

### UF CLI + Speckit/OpenSpec

`uf init` scaffolds 50 files into a repo: personas, specification templates,
convention packs, and governance rules [8]. Speckit provides a 9-phase
strategic pipeline; OpenSpec a lightweight 4-step tactical workflow [8].
Both are OpenCode-specific.

See [references/components.md](references/components.md) for full details.

## 3. Claude Code Compatibility

### What Works

| Component | Claude Code Status | How |
|-----------|-------------------|-----|
| Replicator | **Compatible** | MCP server via stdio [9] |
| Dewey | **Compatible** | MCP server via stdio [10] |
| Gaze | **Partial** | CLI + `--ai=claude` adapter [11] |

Replicator's README includes an explicit Claude Code `mcp_servers`
configuration example [9]. All 53 coordination tools (work tracking,
messaging, worktrees) are accessible from Claude Code through MCP.

### What Doesn't Work

| Component | Reason |
|-----------|--------|
| Hero personas | OpenCode `.opencode/agents/` format [18] |
| Specification commands | OpenCode slash commands [8] |
| Workflow orchestration | OpenCode command system [4] |
| UF CLI scaffolding | Produces OpenCode-specific files [8] |
| Constitution Check gate | Depends on OpenCode workflow [3] |

### Adoption Scenarios

**Full stack**: Not viable — requires OpenCode [8][18].

**Cherry-pick MCP**: Viable — Replicator + Dewey as standalone MCP servers
give Claude Code structured multi-agent coordination and a persistent
knowledge graph. This is the only recommended path.

**Ideas only**: Adopt the patterns without the tooling — constitution-style
enforcement via hooks, review council via parallel subagents, contract
coverage via `gaze` CLI in CI.

See [references/claude-code-compatibility.md](references/claude-code-compatibility.md)
for the full portability matrix and comparison with existing workflow.

## 4. Comparison with Alternatives

### Multi-Agent Orchestration

Replicator is a coordination *protocol* (MCP tools for agents to
self-coordinate); agtx [17] is a coordination *UI* (kanban board for humans
to orchestrate agents). They're complementary, not competing. agtx supports
6 agent types (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot) [17]
and has spec-driven plugins (Spec-Kit, OpenSpec, BMAD, Superpowers) [17].

### Knowledge Management

Dewey provides semantic search + graph traversal + trust tiers [6]; Claude
Code's memory system provides flat markdown files with a 200-line index cap.
This is the clearest capability gap — no Claude Code equivalent exists for
structured knowledge management with lifecycle controls.

### Test Quality

Gaze's contract coverage is a novel concept with no equivalent in any
language [11]. xenon, ruff, and mutmut operate in different problem spaces
(complexity, linting, mutation testing). Gaze uses gocyclo internally [22]
and complements rather than replaces existing tools.

### Specification Frameworks

GitHub Spec-Kit (88.3K stars, 35+ agent support) [16] is a direct competitor
to UF's Speckit and is massively more adopted. UF's value-add is the
governance bridge (constitution alignment check) and tight integration with
the hero persona system.

See [references/alternatives-comparison.md](references/alternatives-comparison.md)
for detailed comparison tables.

The project shows high individual velocity and good engineering practices

## 6. Adoption Risk

### Critical Risks

**Bus factor = 1** [13]: jflowers is the project. If they stop, the project
stops. No governance structure, no foundation backing, no co-maintainers.

**API instability**: Dewey had 3 major version bumps in 14 days (v1→v2→v3)
[14]. Gaze reached v1.0 in 4 days [14]. SemVer [24] says major version 0
means "anything may change at any time" — two of four key repos are still 0.x.

**No community**: 1 star total, no external reviews, no third-party
integrations, no support ecosystem [12].

### Manageable Risks

**OpenCode lock-in**: Low for MCP-only adoption. Replicator and Dewey work
via standard MCP protocol [9][10].

**License**: Apache 2.0 + MIT, fully compatible [25].

**Dependencies**: Lean Go trees, pure-Go SQLite, no CGO [21][22][23].

**Data portability**: SQLite databases, standard export [9][6].

See [references/adoption-risk.md](references/adoption-risk.md) for full risk
matrix and mitigation recommendations.

## Decision Framework

### Should you adopt Unbound Force?

**Step 1**: Are you using OpenCode?
- **No** → Skip the full stack. Evaluate cherry-picked MCP components only.

**Step 2**: Do you need persistent cross-session knowledge management with
semantic search?
- **Yes** → Evaluate Dewey as a standalone MCP server. It's the clearest
  capability gap vs your current Claude Code setup.
- **No** → Claude Code's memory system is sufficient.

**Step 3**: Do you need structured multi-agent coordination (work tracking,
messaging, file reservations)?
- **Yes** → Evaluate Replicator as a standalone MCP server. Compare with
  agtx for your use case.
- **No** → Shell-loop patterns and subagent dispatching are sufficient.

**Step 4**: Do you develop Go projects and care about test quality beyond
coverage?
- **Yes** → Try Gaze. It's standalone, novel, and works with any AI agent.
- **No** → Not relevant (Go-only tool).

**Step 5**: Are you comfortable with the maturity risks?
- Bus factor of 1 [13]
- API may break at any release [14][24]
- No community support [12]
- Project could be abandoned without notice

If yes to Step 5 and any of Steps 2-4: do a time-boxed hands-on evaluation
of the relevant components. Pin exact versions. Have a fallback plan.

## What's Worth Stealing

Even if you don't adopt UF, several ideas are worth incorporating into a
Claude Code workflow:

| Concept | Implementation Path |
|---------|-------------------|
| **Contract coverage** | Run `gaze` in CI for Go projects |
| **Constitution enforcement** | PreToolUse hooks that validate against governance rules |
| **Knowledge lifecycle** | Structured memory files with maturity metadata (draft/validated/authored) |
| **Review council** | Parallel subagent dispatches with different review angles (security, architecture, testing) |
| **Specification governance** | Skills that check proposals against project principles before implementation |

## Limitations of This Research

- Blog post content could not be fetched (404 errors on individual blog URLs) [20]
- Speckit's 9 phases are mentioned but not enumerated in any source [8]
- No performance data (token consumption, latency, cost) for any workflow
- The `ZEN_API_KEY` requirement for Replicator's MCP functionality is unclear [9]
- Dewey's 12 vs 14 category count discrepancy between website and README [6][10]
- Gaze's assertion mapping accuracy (84.7%) is self-reported [7]
- No independent security analysis of any component
